business_scope.primary_industry_name: Customs Clearance Brokerage and Bonded Transit Management

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified commercial and foundation statutes; Private Interest Foundations modeled on the Liechtenstein foundation concept)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012)
Panama–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (in force 2019)
Double Taxation Agreements in force with Mexico, the Netherlands, Spain, South Korea, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Barbados
Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with the United States and EU member states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-money laundering and UBO framework governed by Ley No. 25 de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations, amended by Ley No. 41 de 2013); Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT and beneficial ownership registry); Ley No. 70 de 30 de enero de 2019 (strengthening the Unidad de Análisis Financiero); Decreto Ejecutivo No. 363 de 2015; foundation formation, charter, and registration requirements additionally governed by the Registro Público de Panamá protocols and the customs brokerage licensing regime of the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), including Decree Law 15 of 1992 as amended.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (confidential Registro de Beneficiarios Finales; accessible to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero, judicial authorities, and designated supervisory bodies; not open to public search)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal Panamanian notarial protocol; no apostille required for Panamanian execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founder's Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Members

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the founder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney granted to Panamanian Resident Agent / Counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or certified true copy accepted at ANA / UAF discretion

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening before formation and on an ongoing basis against the UAF list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Panamanian domestic PEP database; PEPs (Ley No. 23 de 2015) trigger Enhanced Due Diligence and senior-management approval; source-of-wealth documentation required for the founder and confirmed beneficiaries; negative news and adverse-media screening required for customs brokerage licensing under ANA fit-and-proper review.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Oficina Virtual (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in Spanish or any language using Latin script, with mandatory transliteration of non-Latin scripts into Latin characters; the registry performs a phonetic search (búsqueda fonética) to reject names identical or confusingly similar to existing entries; a Private Interest Foundation must include a designation such as 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the abbreviation 'PIF' in the corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant files a written reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Director General del Registro Público within 5 business days of notification, followed by an appeal (recurso de apelación) to the Superior Court of the Registro Público; alternatively, a fresh name search with a revised name may be filed immediately; judicial review before the Sala Tercera (Contencioso-Administrativo) of the Corte Suprema de Justicia is available after exhaustion of administrative remedies; all filings must be signed by licensed Panamanian counsel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office not permissible as the statutory registered office: Ley No. 25 de 1995 requires the Foundation to maintain its domicile at the professional address of the Panamanian Resident Agent (licensed attorney or authorized trust/corporate services provider). A back-office virtual arrangement is tolerated for administrative support, but the customs brokerage business must maintain a physical operational office in Panama housing the licensed customs broker, books, and customs archive available for ANA inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registral inspections: low (below 5% per annum for standard foundations); commercial and sanctions inspections: moderate (10-15%); ANA unannounced on-site customs compliance audits: elevated, estimated 35-50% probability within the first 24 months for newly licensed customs brokerage houses; UAF inspections: enhanced for medium-risk regulated sectors and occur at 15-20% per annum on a risk-based cycle.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended, Arts. 1–42, in particular Arts. 9, 14, 23 and 24; residual application of the Código Civil (Civil Code); Executive Decrees regulating the Registro Público fee schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado / Acta Fundacional), registered as a public deed (testimonio) with the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum endowment under Law 25 of 1995; the Charter must state the initial endowment (commonly B/. 10,000.00), which need not be escrowed – funds are credited to the foundation patrimony as book equity; registered agent, Foundation Council and auditor (when required) must be maintained.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME], PANAMA CITY. Whereas the executed Foundation Charter has been inscribed at the Public Registry and the USD 10,000 endowment subscribed; Now, therefore, IT IS RESOLVED: 1. The endowment is accepted and credited to the foundation's patrimony; 2. The registered office is fixed at the offices of the Resident Agent in Panama City; 3. The Resident Agent is ratified; 4. The Foundation Council officers are appointed: President, Treasurer, Secretary; 5. The President and Treasurer are jointly authorized to open bank accounts, file customs brokerage licensing with the National Customs Authority, execute surety bonds, and engage professional advisors; 6. Any ancillary acts are ratified in accordance with Law 25 of 1995.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance, Foundation Charter Drafting and Pre-Notarization Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Panama Emprende online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a name availability search for the proposed Spanish/English foundation name against the Public Registry index. Instruct the drafting attorney to prepare the Foundation Charter in Spanish incorporating: foundation name, registered office, founder nominee, initial endowment, Foundation Council members, beneficiary and protector (if any), and Resident Agent clause. Deliver the charter and questionnaire to a Panamanian notary for notarization.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of the founder/founder nominee
Passport copies of Foundation Council members
Registered Agent acceptance and address undertaking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is identical or confusingly similar to a registered entity, select an alternate name or add a differentiating suffix; resubmit the revised name search and amend the charter before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution and Fiscal Stamp Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Panamá (licensed Panamanian notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Foundation Charter before the chosen notary. Affix the required fiscal stamps (papeleta de timbre fiscal) and municipal stamps based on declared endowment. The notary issues the first testimonio (authenticated public deed copy), which becomes the registration instrument.
required_dossiers: Founder and Council member identification copies
Power of attorney (if founder acts by representative)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags incomplete identity evidence, supply apostilled or consularized passport copies or rectify the power of attorney, then reexecute the deed; no registry impact occurs until filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Central Offices, Panama City)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first testimonio together with the registration fee and any required registry forms. After examination, the Registry issues the certificate of inscription and returns a certified copy (certificado de registro) evidencing the foundation's legal existence. Pay applicable insertion and adjudication fees at the cashier.
required_dossiers: First testimonio of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registry issues a reparos (defect notice), file a corrective clarification or amendment deed through the same notary and resubmit; the inscription will be perfected after adjudication of the corrected instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification (RUC), Municipality Aviso de Operación and Registered Office Physical Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Alcaldía de Panamá / Municipio (Single Window – Panama Emprende for Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the foundation with DGI to obtain the RUC and tax agent credentials, selecting territorial income tax rules and employer obligations. File the Aviso de Operación with the relevant municipality, pay the municipal license fee, and confirm the physical establishment is zoned for office and commission brokerage use (uso de suelo permit).
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the foundation registration
Lease agreement or title for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality queries zoning or domicile, obtain a municipality land-use certificate and rectify the domicile notice; a new Aviso de Operación may be filed for a corrected business address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs Brokerage House License (Aduanas) and Designated Customs Broker Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) – Dirección de Agentes Aduaneros (Customs Brokers Directorate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for the customs agency and brokerage house license (Licencia de Agencia de Aduanas) on behalf of the foundation. Verify that at least one natural-person licensed customs broker is designated to the house and file the statutory customs surety bond. Provide the AML/KYC compliance manual showing the Medium-Risk Enhanced program for broker interfaces (Automated Broker Interface ACH and wire payments). Obtain ANA approval before performing any customs transaction.
required_dossiers: ANA application form for Agencia de Aduanas
Designation contract of the licensed customs broker
Certified copy of foundation charter and RUC
Clean criminal-record certificates of directors and designated broker
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ANA issues an objection on the designated broker or bond, substitute another licensed broker or increase the bond amount and resubmit; appeal adverse determinations through the ANA administrative review within the statutory appeal period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Screening, Fire Safety and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Riesgo Ambiental; Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (Fire Prevention Office); Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil (SINAPROC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the office core of the brokerage house, register with MiAMBIENTE and obtain the environmental registration (ficha de registro) or, if bonded transit or storage areas are operated, file the Category I preliminary environmental risk assessment. Schedule the fire inspection with the Fire Prevention Office to obtain the fire safety certificate for office and any storage area. For bonded warehouses, obtain SINAPROC structural clearance.
required_dossiers: Category I risk assessment (if storage or transit yard exists)
Fire extinguisher and safety equipment inspection report
Structural load certification for storage areas
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where MiAMBIENTE reclassifies the operation to Category II due to warehousing scale, commission a licensed consultant to prepare the full Environmental Impact Study (EsIA); for fire or civil defense defects, remediate per inspection findings and request reinspection before exercising bonded storage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational Safety Registration, Social Security Enrollment and License Portfolio Consolidation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) – Dirección General de Riesgos Profesionales; Caja de Seguro Social (CSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the foundation as an employer with CSS, enroll staff, and file the occupational risk assessment and workplace hygiene and safety program with MITRADEL. Collect all approvals (Registry, DGI, Municipal, ANA, MiAMBIENTE, Bomberos) into the statutory compliance dossier and declare the customs house operational.
required_dossiers: CSS employer registration form and payroll schedule
Staff identity and social security forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MITRADEL inspection cites violations, implement the corrective action plan, obtain reinspection, and submit the compliance certificate; the consolidated dossier is then accepted for operational launch.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) – Dirección de Agentes Aduaneros; Municipalidad de Panamá (Aviso de Operación); Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) as joint authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Agencia de Aduanas (Customs Agency License) together with Municipal Aviso de Operación / Licencia Municipal de Funcionamiento and MiAMBIENTE environmental registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de la República de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Riesgo Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (low impact): Preliminary Environmental Risk Assessment (Ficha de Registro Ambiental) required for office brokerage premises with bonded transit or storage support; pure administrative back-office without storage may qualify for environmental registration only (no full EIA).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office operation with no process discharge: domestic sewage only to municipal sewer; if any wash or pressure facility is installed, wastewater must meet Panamanian discharge norms (pH 6–9, BOD5 ≤ 250 mg/L, TSS ≤ 220 mg/L); VOC emissions negligible; no unpermitted fuel storage; hazardous residues (lubricants, batteries, e-waste) tracked by manifest and transferred to MiAMBIENTE-licensed waste handlers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire prevention certificate issued by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos following on-site inspection (extinguishers, exits, signage); structural load inspection certificate for bonded storage or transit yards (SINAPROC review); occupational health and safety clearance from MITRADEL plus employer registration with the Caja de Seguro Social.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must appoint a resident legal representative and register with the DGI to obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). The application is filed online or through a notary/public registry, presenting foundation charter, apostilled passport/incorporation documents, proof of local address, and the appointed representative's identification. The RUC is issued after verification and is required for ITBMS (VAT) registration, customs operations, and any Panama-sourced taxable activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No federal check-the-box regime; Panama applies territorial taxation. A Private Interest Foundation may elect to be treated as transparent for administrative purposes, but ITBMS registration is compulsory for taxable supply activities. Hybrid mismatch elections under the Multilateral Instrument apply only where Panama has a relevant tax treaty; no domestic deemed-dividend or pay-through election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (VAT/GST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary threshold; any person or entity, including foreign-owned foundations, that engages in taxable supply of goods or services in Panama must register for ITBMS. For small businesses delivering occasional services, annual gross turnover under USD 12,000 may qualify for simplified collection, but customs brokerage services are deemed regular commercial activity and require full registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) is phased in for all VAT-registered taxpayers. Invoices must be transmitted in real time to the DGI's Sede Electrónica via the web portal or an authorized API using XML/JSON format, and each invoice obtains a unique authorization code and QR/digital stamp. Refusal of digital stamping or failure to transmit within the prescribed time (generally 24 hours) triggers fines and disallowance of input VAT credits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the final export of tangible personal property shipped from Panama to a foreign destination, and to services rendered for use wholly outside Panama or directly related to exported goods, provided the foreign customer is legally established outside Panama. Customs brokerage and bonded transit services qualify when physically performed in relation to Panama customs territory but are contractually tied to goods leaving Panama under an export declaration. The taxpayer must keep a file evidencing the actual movement of goods or, for offshore services, a contract plus documentation of performance and payment from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (B/L or Air Waybill, including electronic equivalent from the Panama Customs Single Window)
Inward Remittance Certificate or Bank Proof of Payment from the Non-Resident Customer
DGI Electronic Factura con Código de Autorización stamped for export
Contract or purchase order indicating the offshore destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and Panama Customs Authority conduct coordinated audits of export zero-rating claims. Missing customs declarations, proof of overseas payment, or timely remittance within the 180-day window results in reversal of the zero-rating, immediate collection of ITBMS at 7%, plus surcharge, revaluation, and fines of up to three times the tax amount. Fraudulent issuance of export invoices is criminal tax fraud punishable with imprisonment of two to five years, delisting from the exporter registry, and cancellation of the customs broker license.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank and no foreign exchange administration. The Balboa (PAB) is a purely nominal monetary unit at parity with the US Dollar, which is legal tender under Monetary Regime Law Decree No. 15 of 1904. Banking regulation and supervision are vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) operates as the AML/CFT financial intelligence unit; customs and customs-broker licensing are governed by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA); and Banco Nacional de Panamá serves only as fiscal agent and depositary of the State, not as a monetary authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current-account and capital-account transactions. Panama maintains no exchange-control law, no capital-export permit regime, no foreign-investment registration requirement, and no balance-of-payments clearance. US Dollars may be held, transferred, and remitted freely. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) may distribute profits and endowments to beneficiaries abroad without central bank authorization; the only operational constraint is SBP-regulated bank KYC/AML verification. A PIF conducting customs brokerage in Panama realizes Panamanian-source income subject to territorial taxation (corporate income tax and, where applicable, dividend or distribution withholding), but such obligations are fiscal duties, not currency-convertibility or profit-repatriation hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None apply. Panama imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no central bank deposit requirement for export receipts or service proceeds. USD brokerage fees, commissions, and duty pass-through funds may be retained in full, netted, or freely deployed for working capital. The surrender concept is legally inapplicable in a fully dollarized economy.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD demand deposit with treasury sweep; segregated customs escrow sub-account for client duty monies
Operational USD account; trade finance and supplier-payment lines
Operational USD account; escrow facility for third-party duty collections
Operational USD account; corporate cash management
Operational USD account oriented to international clients and cross-border trade flows
Operational USD account (State fiscal agent; conservative domestic-nexus policy)
Large-corporate operational USD account with global clearing; elevated minimum balances

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium legal viability. Panama has no standalone Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing class; deposit-taking and payment-intermediation require an SBP general or official banking license. Offshore digital EMIs and virtual-account providers (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Mercury, Currencycloud) are not supervised by the SBP or UAF and cannot serve as the primary treasury or customs-duty clearing channel; ANA duty remittances must originate from SBP-licensed banks. Foreign EMIs may be used only as ancillary receivables-collection rails for small overseas clients, subject to an internal concentration cap (not more than 10% of monthly collections), same-day reconciliation into the licensed Panamanian account, and mandatory tagging of each collection to a declared import declaration (DUI).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Risk-based but effectively quasi-physical. SBP regulations do not prohibit remote onboarding, yet Tier-1 Panamanian banks consistently require the physical appearance of at least one authorized foundation council member or a senior attorney-in-fact holding a notarized power of attorney for signature verification; beneficial owners may participate via SBP-compliant live video interview in lower-risk cases, but the medium-risk customs-brokerage classification normally triggers enhanced due diligence and an in-person session for account signatories. The PIF's Panamanian Resident Agent (a licensed attorney) must certify the foundation's valid registration and the council resolution appointing signatories. Fully remote opening is available only at selected institutions (e.g., Towerbank, Global Bank) upon submission of an apostilled and notarized KYC package followed by a video-call interview, and is typically conditional on enhanced transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF opacity risk - confidential foundation deed with undisclosed beneficiaries and nominee-only council.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the foundation deed (acta fundacional) and bylaws; Registered Agent certificate of good standing from the Registro Público de Panamá; final beneficial owner declaration consistent with Panama's centralized Final Beneficial Owner Registry (RBF) under Law 70 of 2019; a signed bank-specific waiver of foundation confidentiality limited to the institution's compliance file; organizational chart of the foundation council and all beneficiary classes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial activity without Panamanian tax and operational nexus - PIF acting as a customs broker but holding no RUC, Aviso de Operación, or ANA license.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ANA customs broker license (Licencia de Agente de Aduanas); Aviso de Operación issued by the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI); taxpayer registration (RUC) issued by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); active customs surety bond (póliza de garantía); foundation council resolution expressly authorizing the commercial activity; statutory financial statements or audited accounts for the prior period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through duty flows - third-party client funds aggregating in the PIF account for customs duties and taxes, raising unlicensed payment-service concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written segregated-escrow accounting policy; executed client mandates identifying each import declaration (DUI) and its corresponding duty amount; daily treasury ledger separating commission income from duty pass-through; independent Panamanian certified public accountant (CPA) attestation of the agency and pass-through nature; ANA settlement receipts evidencing timely liquidation of duties to the public treasury.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: OFAC/sanctions and PEP screening alerts on beneficiaries, trade counterparties, or cargo jurisdictions within a dollarized clearing environment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative-media and sanctions screening reports from a recognized commercial database (World-Check/Refinitiv or equivalent); sworn PEP and non-PEP declarations for all council members and beneficiaries; notarized commercial contracts and a counterparty jurisdiction matrix; cargo and consignee detail pages from the customs declaration system; written undertaking to notify the bank of any ownership or material counterparty change within 30 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed foundation with rapid high-velocity wire turnover inconsistent with declared brokerage scale (potential trade-based money laundering).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth memorandum for the initial endowment supported by 12 months of contributor bank statements; foundation council resolution authorizing account opening and the signatory schedule; 12-month business plan with transaction-velocity projections; expected inbound and outbound counterparty list with country and payment narratives; ANA customs declarations evidencing corresponding trade volumes and commissions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial endowment: SWIFT MT103 from the founder's home bank to the SBP-licensed operational account, with remittance field 70 stating Initial capital contribution - Private Interest Foundation (Ley 25 de 1995) and referencing the foundation deed registration number; sending bank must transmit complete originator data (name, account, address) under Law 23 of 2015 record-keeping and travel-rule obligations. The statutory minimum initial endowment is USD 10,000 (B/.10,000); any inbound contribution above the bank-defined threshold requires source-of-funds documentation before value-dating. Client duty prepayments: SWIFT MT103 or Panama ACH credit referencing the specific DUI number and narrative Customs brokerage fee and duty pass-through; duty monies must land in the segregated escrow sub-account, never the operational account. Panama imposes no mandatory national purpose-code taxonomy, so the MT103 field 70 narrative must fully describe each transaction. Inbound USD from US counterparties moving via the US Automated Broker Interface (ABI) must be treated as data only; the corresponding funds must settle by wire or ACH into the Panamanian account with a matching declaration reference.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Customs duties and taxes: electronic debit instruction or bank collection-window payment to ANA treasury accounts through the ANA electronic declaration and collection portal, funded exclusively from the escrow sub-account. Supplier and logistics payments: SWIFT MT103 (with SWIFT GPI for real-time tracking) for foreign carriers, forwarders, and port terminals; Panama ACH through the Panama Clearing House for domestic operators (transport, warehousing, handling); irrevocable confirmed commercial letters of credit (MT700) for high-value bonded-transit or temporary-import operations requiring documentary security, with the PIF as nominated beneficiary or instructing party as the mandate requires. For US-bound cargo where the PIF clears entries with US CBP, ABI remains a data interface and duty collections must be funded by ACH debit from a pre-funded US clearing account; the Panamanian treasury account must maintain cover for that ACH debit. All outbound wires must cite the DUI, commercial invoice, or LC reference to avoid transactions-unrelated alerts. Same-day USD netting through the local clearing house is permitted for domestic settlement. Commission distributions to foundation council members or beneficiaries must be supported by council distribution minutes and, where Panamanian-source profits are distributed, evidence of satisfaction of any applicable distribution tax.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) with USD cash settlement under ISDA or IFEMA master agreements with SBP-licensed banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD for Latin American currency exposures (COP, MXN, GTQ, CRC) arising from regional logistics payables
Cross-currency swaps (USD versus EUR/GBP) for matched long-term equipment or bonded-facility financings
Vanilla FX call and put options booked with SBP-licensed dealing rooms for receivable-conversion protection
Spot FX executed through licensed interbank desks for same-day conversion of incidental minor-currency receipts
FX netting and same-day sweeps through the Panama Clearing House to minimize conversion frequency and counterparty limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Foundation Fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance – Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), collected through the licensed Foundation Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before September 30 of each calendar year; a first-year fee is pro-rated based on the foundation registration date but must still be paid in accordance with DGI annual schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% immediate late surcharge plus monthly interest accrual up to 100% of the annual fee cap; three consecutive years of non-payment allow the Registro Público to administratively dissolve and strike off the foundation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada Anual de ISR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Panama Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 immediately following the calendar tax year; electronic filing with extension privileges available through DGI-maintained schedules until June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty from USD 50 up to USD 5,000 plus 10% monthly surcharge on unpaid tax; wilful false declarations attract criminal tax penalties of up to twice the omitted tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs Brokerage House License Annual Renewal (Casa de Corredor de Aduanas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) – Panama Customs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through January 31 of each calendar year; concurrent with validation of the customs bond and registered operating address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 25% surcharge for renewals processed in February; renewal after March 31 results in licence suspension and eventual removal from the active customs registry; continued operation without renewal is treated as unauthorised customs agency practice and attracts fines from USD 500 to USD 2,000 per transaction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Standing Confirmation and Confidential Registry Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Transparencia Fiscal – Beneficial Owner Registry, supported by the licensed Foundation Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 for the annual standing confirmation; beneficial owner changes must be recorded within 30 calendar days of the shareholding or control transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning for late confirmation; false or incomplete UBO declarations trigger fines under Panama Law 23 of 2015 and can expose the Foundation Council to judicial audit and criminal enforcement

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for a Panama Private Interest Foundation solely by legal form; compulsory independent audit applies when the foundation conducts Panama-source commercial activity, such as customs brokerage, and annual gross revenue exceeds USD 2,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 5,000,000.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted for Panama for public-interest and large entities; IFRS for SMEs for small and medium entities; books are kept in Spanish and accounting papers must be available for DGI inspection.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation Agent must verify the foundation's underlying ownership and control structure and file a confidential annual standing confirmation with Panama's beneficial owner registry by March 31; any transfer of economic rights requires a revised UBO chart and notarial/minute-book annotation filed within 30 days of the transfer. No public UBO disclosure is made by the Registro Público.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members and Resolutions
Register of Attendance and Minutes of Foundation Council Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – 1,200 per annum (Panama registered agent for the Foundation plus compliance management with DGI and ANA)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 6,000 for a certified audit when the compulsory audit threshold is exceeded; below-threshold entities can rely on internal reviewed financial statements at approximately USD 1,200 – 2,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies territorial corporate income tax to Panama-source income only. There is no general income tax holiday for a customs brokerage house; relief is limited to licensed regime participants such as Colon Free Zone operators, Panama Pacifico SEM licensees, and City of Knowledge users. Deductions are restricted to expenses directly incurred in generating Panama-source income. Foreign-source receipts and capital gains on non-Panama assets are excluded. Net operating losses may be carried forward 5 years. The Simplified Regime (SIM) is only available to small taxpayers with gross revenue below B/.1,000,000 and is not presumed available to a licensed customs brokerage house.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 202 (Declaración Anual del Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed through the Panama DGI e-tax portal Sistema TAN/alternate e-tax at etax.dgi.gob.pa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the return and payment are due on or before 31 March unless DGI publishes an extension requiring payment of a minimum advance portion of assessed tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares the opening and closing dates of the fiscal year covered by the return. The period must match the accounting cycle registered with the DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Private Interest Foundation or foreign-owned Panama customs brokerage must use the same fiscal year as its registered Panama entity. If no Panama-source income exists, a nil return with 'Sin actividades generadoras de renta panameña' is required to preserve Paz y Salvo.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Ingresos Gravables de Fuente Panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports all gross Panama-source income from customs brokerage fees, clearance services, bonded transit supervision, storage, and ancillary logistics services performed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate foreign-source compensation with dated contracts, place-of-performance evidence, and bank receipts. Income is recharacterized as Panama-source if personnel, servers, or operational management are physically located in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records deductions for salaries, rent, utilities, customs bond premiums, professional fees, software, depreciation, and other expenses directly allocable to Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses borne by the Panama taxpayer and paid by traceable bank transfers are deductible. Payments made from non-resident personal accounts or through informal value transfer systems are disallowed and trigger withholding and payroll adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes net taxable income after deductible costs. A negative result becomes an operating loss available for the 5-year carryforward under Panama territorial tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF or foreign-owned customs brokerage with zero Panama-source income must file zero. Any loss must be supported by a monthly general ledger, statutory accounts, and local invoice files in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 20 - Impuesto sobre la Renta Determinado
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applies the 25% statutory corporate income tax rate to net taxable income, then credits prepayments, withholding credits, advance payments, and eligible dividend tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If territorial CIR is nil, enter zero. No foreign tax credit or treaty credit may be claimed unless a DTA relief application and Form 211 credit request has been accepted by DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 26 - Pagos Anticipados, Retenciones y Créditos
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Lists Form 203 monthly or quarterly advance payments, DGI assessments, customer withholding certificates, and dividend tax credit accruals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach copies of Form 203 receipts and customer withholding certificates issued by Panamanian payors. The personal taxes of non-resident shareholders or foundation beneficiaries cannot be claimed as corporate credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Completes the related-party transaction schedule and designated transfer pricing method for cross-border or domestic related-party dealings, including customs brokerage fees paid to or received from a linked PIF or logistics affiliate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for each related party, with contracts, PAN/TIN records, banking evidence, and an OECD-aligned arm's-length analysis. If the entity has nil operations, submit a nil TP schedule only when no related-party transactions exist.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 202 by the statutory deadline triggers Fiscal Code late-filing fines, surcharges calculated on the tax due, monthly late-payment interest, loss of Paz y Salvo, suspension of the RUC, and blockage of customs license renewal. Continuing nonfiling exposes directors and the licensed customs broker to DGI criminal complaint and license revocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 203 (Anticipos del Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed through the DGI e-tax portal; applicable to taxpayers subject to advance payments during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 15 days after the close of each prepayment period; licensed customs brokerages are normally assigned monthly or quarterly prepayment calendars by DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the calendar month or quarter to which the advance payment corresponds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must ensure the Panamanian fiscal agent calculates the advance based on the immediately preceding tax return and current-year projected Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports the anticipated taxable income base and applies the effective advance rate notified by DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If actual income is zero, the taxpayer should file a nil anticipo to avoid DGI automated assessments and interest accrual.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted advance payments accrue daily interest and surcharges from the original due date and may cause DGI to calculate the annual Form 202 tax without credit for prepayments, resulting in a locked refund position and compulsory collection.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends distributed by a Panamanian corporation out of taxable Panama-source profits; a reduced incremental 5% rate may apply under the dividend-tax-credit mechanism when the distributing corporation can prove that underlying profits were fully taxed at the 25% territorial CIR and the distribution satisfies the Fiscal Code credit-attribution rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Panama income tax treaty, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign competent authority and submit it, together with a Form 211 treaty-relief request, beneficial-ownership declaration, audited ownership chart, commercial registry extract, and a copy of the contract, to the DGI before or at the time of filing the annual return. The DGI examines limitation-on-benefits and principal-purpose test provisions; absent a valid TRC and full beneficial-ownership disclosure, the statutory withholding rate applies. Approved treaty relief may reduce dividend, interest, or royalty withholding rates to the rate specified in the relevant DTA, commonly 5% to 10% for dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid from Panama-source use of intellectual property, software, industrial know-how, or trademarks to a non-resident are subject to a 10% statutory gross-basis withholding tax; technical-assistance fees packaged as royalties are often recharacterized at the same or a 12.5% rate. Interest paid by a Panama obligor to a non-resident lender not engaged in Panama banking is generally subject to 4% statutory withholding, while interest on qualified bank deposits, bonded-zone financing, and certain international loan facilities may be exempt. Under applicable DTAs, royalty rates generally fall to 10%, and interest rates may fall to 4% or 5% subject to beneficial ownership and anti-abuse conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous Local File and Master File preparation is triggered when the Panamanian taxpayer's annual gross revenue exceeds B/.2,000,000 (Balboa/USD at par) or its related-party transactions in a fiscal year exceed B/.250,000 per related party. A stricter B/.100,000 threshold applies to transactions with a related party resident in a zero-tax or non-cooperative jurisdiction. A Country-by-Country Report to the DGI is required for MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least USD 750,000,000; the TP annex must be filed with the annual return or by the DGI-determined supplementary date.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama applies Economic Substance Regulations and substance-over-form doctrine to tax residents and licensed juridical persons. A licensed customs brokerage house is not a passive PIF entity; its core income-generating activities must be performed in Panama through a licensed operational office, qualified staff, local board meetings, actual decision-making, and adequate expenses and physical assets. Holding a customs brokerage license through a foundation with nominee directors and no commercial activity is a shell arrangement and will be disregarded for tax purposes. The PIF holding structure may own the customs brokerage, but the brokerage itself must demonstrate real presence, employment, and operational substance independent of its foreign beneficiaries.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Customs Declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting Panama-source brokerage commissions from Form 202; issuing or receiving false invoices for fictitious clearance services; undervaluing imported goods; using a PIF as a conduit to shift Panama-source income through fake off-shore invoices; and destroying ledgers or customs records during an audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil tax penalties equal to a substantial percentage of the evaded tax, daily late-payment interest, revocation of Paz y Salvo, suspension of the customs broker license, confiscation of goods, and criminal tax evasion charges with imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and fines of two to three times the evaded amount under the Panama Fiscal Code and Penal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced where the PIF or brokerage is found to be a mere instrumentality. Directors, the resident agent, and the licensed customs broker are jointly liable for unpaid taxes and penalties when they signed false returns, directed false invoicing, or knowingly participated in smuggle-friendly operations. Criminal conviction may trigger travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Beneficial Ownership Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation with nominee founders and beneficiaries, nonexistent local staff, no physical office, no board resolutions, and no separate accounting for the customs brokerage; presenting a dormant PIF as the real owner of a brokerage to hide the ultimate beneficial owner and strip the licensing requirement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may disregard the foundation, attribute the brokerage income directly to the beneficial owner, assess the 25% CIR plus penalties, revoke the RUC and customs license, and administratively dissolve the entity. Failure to file accurate beneficial ownership information under Law 23 of 2015 and the Corporate Transparency regulations exposes the entity to fines, registration cancellation, and criminal sanctions for false declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, foundation council members, and the registered agent who sign false beneficial ownership declarations or conceal ultimate owners are personally liable for civil restitution and fines. Courts may issue travel bans, disbar the licensed customs broker, and impose imprisonment for money laundering and fraudulent misrepresentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Trade-Based Money Laundering, and Illegal Payment Channeling
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large cash deposits for customs services without filing the Law 23 of 2015 currency transaction report; structuring Automated_Broker_Interface ACH or wire payments to evade transaction thresholds; failing to report suspicious transactions to the Panama Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF); processing brokerage payments on behalf of clients engaged in contraband, drug trafficking, or terrorist financing; and using the customs brokerage account to move funds without any underlying customs declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of B/.50,000 to B/.1,000,000 or more for non-financial designated entities, license revocation, closure of the operational office, and confiscation of funds. Criminal conviction for trade-based money laundering carries imprisonment of 5 to 12 years and fines equal to the laundered amount or its equivalent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and customs brokers are individually liable for knowingly failing to file suspicious transaction reports, allowing wire-payment structuring, or participating in trade-based laundering. Sanctions include personal asset seizure, travel bans, director disqualification, and imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced for AML liabilities under Panamanian law when the entity is used as an instrument of crime.
